sources.locator: Chapter 12 §§12.1–12.5.1, PDF pp. 162–168 (printed pp. 153–161): heat-step truncation, method of lines, stability, the convergence error recurrence (12.18), and PDE-versus-ODE stability discussion.

contents.name: Example 12.1, local truncation error for forward-Euler heat stencil (12.5)
contents.reason: The assigned heat examples use a diagonal spectral-grid realization rather than this three-point spatial stencil; their local defects are calculated directly in the common-space norm.

contents.name: Method of lines heat discretization and its finite-dimensional ODE system
contents.reason: The local restriction/reconstruction interface represents a finite-dimensional grid update inside one Banach-space scheme and states the exact complement-invariance condition needed for its powers.

contents.name: Example 12.2, explicit heat Euler stability restriction k/h^2 <= 1/2
contents.reason: The example motivates the stable/unstable heat contrast; its actual spectral-grid multipliers and common-space instability are a different family and are verified locally rather than inferred from this CFL bound.

contents.name: Section 12.4, stiffness ratio of the heat method-of-lines matrix
contents.reason: The pair states no stiffness, work-count, or implicit-step claim; only the exact consistency and common-norm power bounds enter the equivalence theorem.

contents.name: Section 12.3, stability theory for mesh-dependent ODE matrices
contents.reason: The source emphasizes mesh-dependent operators; the local lemma proves exactly which uniform restriction, reconstruction and norm-comparison bounds transfer grid power stability to the common space.

contents.name: Equation (12.18), telescoping global-error estimate
contents.reason: The local proof writes and verifies the operator telescoping identity, then bounds its sum on the dense invariant subspace and extends by density.

contents.name: Section 12.5, convergence and Lax Equivalence statement
contents.reason: This is the independent second treatment of the theorem; the notes state that a complete proof is elsewhere and give (12.18), while the local proof supplies both directions in the declared common-space norm.

contents.name: Section 12.5.1, PDE versus ODE stability scaling
contents.reason: This discussion concerns spatial eigenvalue growth and timestep restrictions; the assigned theorem uses an exact uniform power bound and does not claim a spectral or CFL criterion.
